summary: At just 1.6 square miles, Lemon Hill packs nearly 15,000 people into a density that rivals some inner-city neighborhoods — over 9,300 residents per square mile — yet it's technically an unincorporated census-designated place wedged into Sacramento County's urban fabric south of the city of Sacramento, not a city at all. That distinction matters: there's no city council, no municipal services layer, and county governance shapes everything from road maintenance to code enforcement. The flat Sacramento Valley floor here offers wide-open skies and reliable sunshine — averaging 9.6 hours of daylight daily — with warm summers pushing daytime highs well above the 76°F annual average and mild winters rarely dipping below the low 50s at night. A median home value of $328,000 against a median household income of roughly $49,400 yields a price-to-income ratio around 6.6, meaning purchasing requires significant stretching even at these prices, which sit far below Sacramento metro norms. Rents at $1,376 consume roughly a third of that median income before taxes. The poverty rate of 28.3% reflects an economy leaning heavily on service-sector and public-sector employment, with most professional jobs requiring a commute north into Sacramento proper or toward Rancho Cordova. Lemon Hill is a place where Sacramento's affordability gap and governance structure collide on a very small map.
